name: SkillEvaluator
description: Multi-tier framework for evaluating AI agent skills and plugins with quality gates, semantic overlap detection, synthetic evaluation dataset generation, and live agent evaluation that measures how skills affect agent behavior.
readmeExcerpt:
# SkillEvaluator > 📺 **Livestream:** [Ask the Experts: Evaluating Agent Skills](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4rI0zATFxYI) SkillEvaluator checks AI agent skills and measures their effect on task results: start with quality checks, then compare runs with and without a skill. Agent skills are folders of instructions and supporting files defined by the [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/). SkillEvaluator is part of the [NVIDIA Verified Skills pipeline](https://github.com/NVIDIA/skills). ## Get started Three ways in, one CLI, same results.
1. Run the CLI directly 2. Add it to your repo via CI 3. Wire it to your agent
Install with pip: ```bash pip install skillevaluator ```
Or install with uv ```bash uv tool install \ skillevaluator ```
Then check your skill, no API key: ```bash skillevaluator validate \ ./my-skill --tiers 1 ``` Other tiers: [installation guide](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/installation). 		Run this in your GitHub repository. It opens a setup PR: ```bash skillevaluator ci init ``` GitLab and details: [repository guide](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/repository-integration). Add the skill to Claude Code, Codex or another agent: ```bash npx skills add \ NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator ``` Then ask: *"Is my skill any good?"* It runs the CLI from step 1. See the [agent guide](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/agent-skill).
## Quickstart Both paths use bundled `text-analyzer`. | Start here | Requires | First result | | --- | --- | --- | | [Run without an LLM](#run-without-an-llm) | Git and uv | A deterministic quality score and findings | | [Use NVIDIA Build](#use-nvidia-build) | Git, uv, and a Build API key | Model-backed rubric scores and feedback | Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) and Git, then get the example: ```bash git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator.git cd SkillEvaluator ``` uv provisions Python 3.13 and dependencies. For standalone installation, see [Installation](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/installation). ### Run without an LLM ```bash uv run --python 3.13 skillevaluator quality-check \ src/skillevaluator/tier3/reference_skills/text-analyzer \ -r cli -r json -o reports/first-quality ``` No API key, scanner, GPU or Docker is needed. The example scores **88.8/100 (B)**, exits `0` and saves `reports/first-quality/skillevaluator-quality.json`. The passing threshold defaults to 70. This checks static quality; publication evidence stays `INCOMPLETE`. Security needs scanners; agent impact needs live evaluation. Replace the example path with your skill directory. See the [keyless walkthrough](docs/quickstart.mdx#run-without-an-llm). ### Use NVIDIA Build Eligible NVIDIA Developer Program members can use NVIDIA-hosted endpoints for **free prototyping**, subject to [access terms and rate limits](https://docs.api.nvidia.com/nim/docs/product). 1. Sign in at [build.nvidia.com](https://build.nvidia.com/) and complete enrollment. 2. Open a model page, select **Get API Key**, and generate your key. 3. Set the provider and key in the same terminal, then run the rubric check: ```bash export SKILL_EVAL_LLM_PROVIDER=nv_build export NVIDIA_API_KEY='nvapi-...' uv run --python 3.13 --extra llm skillevaluator rubric-eval \ src/skillevaluator/tier3/reference_skills/text-analyzer \ -r cli -r json -o reports/first-build ``` The command sends skill documentation to the model and saves feedback in `reports/first-build/skillevaluator-rubric.json`. No agent runtime or Docker is needed. Completed evaluations can still fail rubric thresholds. The same key supports Tier 2 embeddings and supported Tier 3 agents. See the [Build walkthrough](docs/quickstart.mdx#use-nvidia-build) or [provider configuration](docs/configuration.mdx). ## Three-tier overview Each tier is independent. Add its extra to your command: | Tier | Question | Example after setup | Additional setup | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Tier 1: Validation | Is the skill safe, well-formed and [harness-compatible](docs/tier1-validation.mdx#the-checks)? | `uv run skillevaluator tier1 ./my-skill --no-llm` | External scanners for full static coverage; a provider and model clients enable LLM checks | | Tier 2: Deduplication | Does guidance repeat or overlap? | `uv run --extra tier2 skillevaluator tier2 ./my-skill` | Embeddings and chat; add `--catalog ./skill-catalog.json` for inter-skill comparison | | Tier 3: Live Evaluation | Does the skill help the agent? | `uv run --extra tier3 skillevaluator tier3 ./my-skill` | Provider access, a supported agent, and a running sandbox (Docker by default) | Tier 1 fetches pinned, verified SkillSpector and Gitleaks releases when they are missing; Semgrep is optional. See [scanners](docs/installation.mdx#system-tools). `--no-llm` does not remove scanner requirements; a scanner that cannot run is `INCOMPLETE` and exits nonzero. [SkillSpector](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillSpector) provides specialized skill security scanning; [Harbor](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor), the open-source agent evaluation framework, powers sandboxed agent runs. Tier 2 reports when inter-skill comparison did not run. Tier 3 autopilot reuses sources or creates one skill-grounded case with limited coverage. See [tier guides](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/). ## Run the combined pipeline After setting up the provider, scanners, and agent sandbox, run all three tiers: ```bash uv run --python 3.13 --extra all skillevaluator doctor --env-mode docker uv run --python 3.13 --extra all skillevaluator validate ./my-skill ``` `doctor` checks readiness, not inference success. `validate` runs all tiers with autopilot for skills. Use `--tiers 1,2` to skip live evaluation or `--tiers 1` for static checks. `--no-autopilot` requires an existing source. Other artifact types retain their applicable stages. Tier 1 gates `validate`. Tier 2 gates unless `--no-block-on-dedup` is set; Tier 3 gates only with `--block-on-agent-eval`. Model and managed-sandbox usage can incur charges; see [runtime and cost](docs/tier3-live-evaluation.mdx#plan-for-cost). Standalone generation needs substantive `evals/EVAL.md` guidance, a `--prompt` file with task requests and outcomes, or matching retained traces. `--force` below replaces the autopilot starter; `--refine` refines it. Explicit `--grounding skill` permits skill-only starters. Review cases; templates omit unauthored negatives. ```bash uv run --python 3.13 --extra tier3 skillevaluator tier3 create-eval-dataset ./my-skill --full --prompt eval-guidance.md --force ``` ## Run from a source checkout Use `uv run --python 3.13` with the relevant extra. See [Installation](docs/installation.mdx#choosing-extras) for extras and standalone upgrades. ## Research and citation Resources: [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.20614), [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.20614), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2608.20614), [BibTeX](https://arxiv.org/bibtex/2608.20614), and the [NVIDIA Developer blog](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/evaluating-ai-agent-skill-performance-with-nvidia-skillevaluator/). Cite the paper and record the SkillEvaluator release or commit; see [CITATION.cff](CITATION.cff). ## Documentation See [the documentation](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/) for setup, tier guides, reports, CI integration, CLI reference, and [performance dashboard](docs/reports.mdx#performance-dashboard). ## Installation and third-party software Follow the [installation guide](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/installation) to choose the full installation or a smaller per-tier setup. This project will download and install additional third-party open source software projects. Review the license terms of these open source projects before use. ## Contributing Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and run: ```bash make lint && make test && make build ``` See [project governance](GOVERNANCE.md) and the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). ## Support Support level: **Experimental**. Community-supported, best-effort, with no SLA or NVIDIA enterprise support entitlement. Report bugs and feature requests through [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/issues); see [SUPPORT.md](SUPPORT.md). ## Security Report suspected vulnerabilities using the private process in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). Do not disclose security issues in a public GitHub issue. ## Releases Release changes are recorded in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) and [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/releases). ## License Apache License 2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE), [NOTICE](NOTICE), and [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.

releases.name: SkillEvaluator 0.9.0
releases.body:
# SkillEvaluator 0.9.0

SkillEvaluator 0.9.0 expands how you build evaluation datasets, compare skill versions, and understand why an agent passed or failed. It adds controls for evaluation budgets, reusable baselines, and clearer evidence across terminal, HTML, JSON, Markdown, and benchmark reports.

For PyPI users upgrading from 0.7.2, this release also includes the changes shipped in the GitHub-only 0.8.0 release.

## Highlights

- **Build and review better evaluation datasets.** Declare deterministic checks for script execution, workspace files, and final responses. Generate datasets grounded in skill instructions, author intent, or traces; import production traces as redacted review candidates; and promote expectations only after explicit human review. Preview legacy dataset migrations before writing a new file.
- **Track skill improvements over time.** Compare retained skill versions with `--compare-to` and `compare-versions`, browse run history, and reuse a compatible no-skill baseline with `--reuse-baseline`. Version comparisons remain separate from Skill Lift against a no-skill baseline.
- **Control evaluation spending.** Set token, judge-call, attempt, and priced-cost bud

releases.name: SkillEvaluator v0.8.0
releases.body:
# SkillEvaluator 0.8.0

Tier 3 now computes every score from judge verdicts, grades accuracy on the outcome alone, and explains failing scores in the HTML report. A new `tier3 feedback` chat answers questions about a completed run, and opt-in policies control which models a judge may fall back to. Reports give every finding stable IDs. Tier 1 accepts audited SkillSpector baselines and evidence-bound PII waivers. This release also ships a rebuilt Tier 1 scanner image and CI bundle.

```bash
pip install --upgrade skillevaluator
skillevaluator ci init
```

[PyPI package](https://pypi.org/project/skillevaluator/0.8.0/) · [CLI onboarding guide](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/cli-onboarding) · [Ready-to-use CI templates](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/tree/v0.8.0/ci/bundles/0.8.0)

## Before you upgrade

- **The shared validation policy is now `default`** ([#334](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/pull/334)). The shared OSS policy for public and private repositories was called `external`. `--profile external`, `--external`, and `SKILLEVALUATOR_PROFILE=external` still work, with the same rules. releases.body:
# SkillEvaluator 0.7.2

Add hosted reports to an existing GitHub skill-checks workflow while keeping its shared component, folders, thresholds, and triggers. A centrally maintained component such as `@v3` can now update its pinned evaluator without requiring an edit in every consumer repository. Each report retains the signed evaluator identity and resolved workflow revisions.

```bash
pip install --upgrade skillevaluator
skillevaluator ci init
```

[PyPI package](https://pypi.org/project/skillevaluator/0.7.2/) · [CLI onboarding guide](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/cli-onboarding) · [Ready-to-use CI templates](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/tree/v0.7.2/ci/bundles/0.7.2)

## GitHub onboarding and reporting

- Preserve an existing supported scan workflow while adding hosted HTML and one updated PR comment. Direct evaluator calls and shared-component calls are supported.
- Verify the shared component's identity permission before changing repository settings. Existing Actions restrictions, unrelated Pages sites, and deployment approvals remain protected.
- Reuse an administrator-configured private Pages site in eligible GitHub Enterprise Cloud organization rep

## Highlights

- Set up repository checks with `skillevaluator ci init`; use `ci status` to inspect setup and `ci demo` to open an optional test PR.

releases.body:
# SkillEvaluator 0.7.0

SkillEvaluator 0.7.0 adds Python 3.14 support alongside Python 3.12 and 3.13, reusable Tier 1 CI integration, configurable quality policies, and clearer evaluation reports.

## Highlights

- Python 3.14 support, with full-suite CI and built-package installation checks across Python 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14.
- Reusable GitHub Actions and GitLab CI checks, parallel skill scanning, and configurable quality headings and thresholds.
- Verdict-led HTML reports, case-first Tier 3 summaries, matching-judge comparisons, and actionable recommendations in `what_to_fix.json`.
- More precise Tier 2 completeness reporting, Tier 3 timeout/recovery and local-mode fixes, and an optional `--max-cases` limit for exploratory runs.
- SkillSpector 2.13.3 installation and CI pins, preserved NVIDIA Build model-registry handling, and validated LLM provenance in JSON/HTML reports.
- Refreshed locked runtime and dashboard dependencies. The Python package's dependency ranges are unchanged.

aiSummary.oneLiner: Multi‑tier framework that validates AI agent skills and quantifies their effect on task performance
aiSummary.whatItDoes: SkillEvaluator addresses the lack of systematic quality and impact assessment for AI agent skills defined by the Agent Skills specification. It implements a three‑tier pipeline—static validation, semantic deduplication, and live agent evaluation—each optional and runnable via a single CLI. Tier 1 runs safety and format checks using SkillSpector, Gitleaks, and optional Semgrep without requiring an LLM. Tier 2 computes embedding‑based overlap to detect redundant guidance across a catalog of skills. Tier 3 executes the skill in a sandboxed agent (Harbor) and measures performance changes, optionally using NVIDIA Build LLMs for rubric scoring. The framework produces deterministic JSON or CLI reports and can be integrated in CI or invoked programmatically.
keyFeatures: Tier‑1 validation: Performs safety, format, and harness compatibility checks with SkillSpector and Gitleaks without an LLM.
Tier‑2 deduplication: Uses embedding models to detect semantic overlap between a skill and a catalog, flagging redundant guidance.
Tier‑3 live evaluation: Runs the skill in a sandboxed agent environment and reports impact on task success metrics.
CLI integration: Single command interface supports pip, uv, and CI workflows, producing JSON and human‑readable outputs.
Provider flexibility: Works keyless or with NVIDIA Build, allowing LLM‑backed rubric scoring via environment variables.

useCases.title: CI quality gate for skill repositories
useCases.description: Teams can add `skillevaluator ci init` to their GitHub pipelines to automatically reject skills that fail static safety or format checks before merge.

useCases.title: Skill marketplace curation
useCases.description: Marketplace operators run the full three‑tier pipeline to ensure submitted skills are non‑redundant and demonstrably improve agent performance, providing a quantitative grade.

useCases.title: Research benchmarking of agent capabilities
useCases.description: Researchers generate synthetic evaluation datasets with `tier3 create-eval-dataset` and compare how different skill sets affect benchmark tasks.

useCases.title: Secure plugin development
useCases.description: Developers of agent plugins use Tier 1 scans to catch insecure code patterns and missing license headers early in the development cycle.

useCases.title: Custom agent integration
useCases.description: Deployers add the skill to Claude Code or Codex via `npx skills add` and let the agent query SkillEvaluator to decide whether to use the skill at runtime.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: SkillEvaluator is aimed at AI agent developers, skill marketplace curators, and CI engineers who need automated quality and impact testing of Agent Skills. Users should be comfortable with Python, command‑line tools, and optionally have access to NVIDIA Build API keys for LLM‑backed rubrics.
